fields.reasoning: Milestone 35's statement names a 40-minute ship-change run, and m35-ship-40m is its measurable done point; the perf report (~/orchestrator/perf-2026-11-12/report-prospective.md, item 1) puts gate and gate-fix at ~25m per run and says no m35 change set covers it, so the change set serves that done point rather than m4-runs-hold-up (about hand repair, which the sibling's trigger change fits). internal/api/ship_gate.go already skips the gate when HEAD equals the recorded Gated head on a clean tree; the intent's 4 reruns in run 01M787SV followed rendered-model and .rhiza/log changes, which change HEAD but not code, so keying the reuse on the non-.rhiza/ tree hash (option 1 of the intent) removes them while any code change still reruns it. Leaving .rhiza/ out is safe because the pre-push check runs rhiza check and make self-check before every push regardless. The intent's point (3) and m32-go-in-own-workflows require Go behaviour to live in Rhiza's own config, so the product only hands the command its base and the per-language scoping lives in this repo's gate command, with a full-suite fallback so a scoping gap never lets an untested change through.
fields.statement: Change set 01M78T0 serves m35-ship-40m (milestone 35: a ship-change run takes 40 minutes or less). Reuse: ship gate records, beside the head it passed on (ship state Gated), the hash of that head's tree with the top-level .rhiza/ entry left out, and passes at once without running the gate when the branch's current HEAD, with a clean worktree, has the same non-.rhiza/ tree hash; any change outside .rhiza/ (a conflict fix, a merge of origin/main that brings code) reruns it. .rhiza/ changes are already checked on every push by the pre-push check (rhiza check, then rhiza.ship.prePushCheck). Scope: Rhiza stays language-neutral. The gate command remains the project's setting rhiza.ship.localGate; ship gate runs it with the base it compares against in the environment (RHIZA_GATE_BASE, the merge-base with origin/main, and RHIZA_GATE_HEAD), and the project's command does the scoping. This repo sets its gate to a script/make target of its own that tests the Go packages the branch changes since that base, their reverse dependencies, the affected testscripts and make self-check, falling back to the full suite when it cannot work out the scope (or the base is missing); the full suite stays with CI. No Go-specific scoping goes into the shipped product.
